vocabulary.meaning_en: to say what is bad about someone or something
having a natural ability to do something well
work done to help the public, e.g. hospitals, schools
vocabulary.example: Buses are an important public service.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a disease that spreads over the whole world
a person who is just starting to learn something
a piece of work you must do
vocabulary.example: I have three tasks to finish today.
The minister is an important person.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a lot of control or influence
a sudden dangerous situation that needs action
a very famous person admired by many; an old story
the time a person is alive
vocabulary.example: It was the trip of a lifetime.

fine_lines.title: Key worker vs frontliner
fine_lines.explanation_ar: key worker شخص يقدّم خدمة أساسية للمجتمع مثل المعلّم والطبيب وسائق الحافلة. frontliner شخص يعمل مباشرة في مواجهة الخطر أو الأزمة، مثل الأطباء والمسعفين.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A key worker provides an essential service (teacher, nurse, bus driver). A frontliner works directly in the dangerous situation, face to face with the crisis (doctors, paramedics).

examples.sentence: Teachers were key workers during the pandemic.
As a paramedic, she's a frontliner.

fine_lines.title: Whizz-kid vs noob
fine_lines.explanation_ar: whizz-kid شاب ذكي جداً وناجح في مجال معيّن. noob شخص مبتدئ قليل الخبرة يرتكب أخطاء بسيطة. معنيان متعاكسان تقريباً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A whizz-kid is a young, very clever and successful person. A noob is a beginner who makes simple mistakes. They are almost opposites.

examples.sentence: The 16-year-old computer whizz-kid built his own app.
I'm a total noob at chess.

fine_lines.title: Bigwig vs legend in one's lifetime
fine_lines.explanation_ar: bigwig شخص مهم وذو نفوذ في مؤسسة (غير رسمية وأحياناً ساخرة). a legend in one's lifetime شخص مشهور جداً ومحبوب وهو ما يزال على قيد الحياة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A bigwig is an important, powerful person in an organisation (informal, a bit jokey). 'A legend in their own lifetime' is someone very famous and admired while still alive.

examples.sentence: Some bigwigs from head office are visiting today.
That scientist became a legend in her own lifetime.

expressions.meaning_en: a person who dislikes something strongly, or always criticises others
expressions.example: Don't listen to the haters - your work is great.

expressions.meaning_en: a young person who is very clever and successful at something
expressions.example: Our new accountant is a real whizz-kid with numbers.

expressions.meaning_en: a person whose job gives an essential service to society
expressions.example: Nurses, bus drivers and shop staff are key workers.

expressions.meaning_en: (informal) a person who is new to something and has little experience
expressions.example: Sorry, I'm a noob - how do I join the video call?

expressions.meaning_en: a person who does many very small online tasks for tech companies, usually for little money
expressions.example: Microworkers label photos to help train computer systems.
All the bigwigs from the company came to the meeting.

expressions.meaning_en: a person working directly with the public in a crisis, e.g. a doctor or nurse
expressions.example: Frontliners in hospitals worked very long hours.

expressions.meaning_en: a person who is very famous and admired while still alive
expressions.example: That old footballer is a legend in his own lifetime.

grammar.title: Making nouns for people
grammar.explanation_ar: نصنع أسماء الأشخاص بطرق مختلفة: بإضافة er- إلى الفعل (hate → hater، work → worker)، أو بدمج كلمتين (whizz + kid، front + line + er، big + wig). نتذكر أن e في نهاية الفعل لا تُكرَّر: hate → hater.
grammar.explanation_en: We make nouns for people by adding -er to a verb (hate → hater, work → worker) or by joining words (whizz + kid, front line + -er, big + wig). If the verb ends in -e, just add -r: hate → hater.

questions.question: A 'hater' is someone who:
questions.explanation_ar: hater = شخص يكره أو ينتقد دائماً.
questions.explanation_en: A hater dislikes or criticises things.

questions.question: A 14-year-old who builds robots is a ___ .
questions.explanation_en: A whizz-kid is young and very clever.

questions.question: Teachers and bus drivers are ___ because their work is essential.
questions.explanation_ar: key worker = عامل يقدم خدمة أساسية.

questions.question: People who do tiny online jobs, like tagging photos, are ___ .
questions.explanation_ar: microworker = عامل مهام صغيرة على الإنترنت.
questions.explanation_en: Microworkers do very small online tasks.

questions.question: The director and other ___ came to the opening.
Which person works directly in a crisis, like a paramedic?
questions.explanation_ar: frontliner يعمل مباشرة في مواجهة الأزمة.
questions.explanation_en: A frontliner works face to face with the crisis.

questions.question: 'She's a legend in her own lifetime' means she is:
choices: a character in an old story
questions.explanation_ar: a legend in one's lifetime = مشهور ومحبوب وهو حيّ.
questions.explanation_en: Famous and admired while still alive.

questions.question: Which two words are almost OPPOSITES?
questions.explanation_en: A whizz-kid is very skilled; a noob is a beginner.

questions.question: Choose the correct person noun: 'He hates everything. He's a real ___ .'
questions.explanation_ar: hate تنتهي بـ e فنضيف r فقط: hater.
